title: Saying what you do

grammar.title: Present tense: ka- + person prefix
grammar.body:
Regular present-tense verbs take **ka-** plus a person prefix. Learn one pattern, get every verb:
| person | prefix | eat (akol) | drink (shreb) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | kan- | kanakol | kanshreb |
| you | kat- | katakol | katshreb |
| he/it | kay- | kayakol | kayshreb |
Make it negative by wrapping it: **ma** kanakol**sh** (I don't eat).
Four words break the pattern but do the heavy lifting — memorize them as-is: **bghit** (I want), **khessni** (I need), **3andi** (I have), **kayn** (there is).

canDo: Form regular present-tense verbs for I, you, and he/it
Say what you eat, drink, want, need, and are looking for

items.note: kanqelleb 3la l-otel = I'm looking for the hotel.
The 'you' form — recognize it in questions.
Fixed form. + noun or verb: bghit atay / bghit nemshi (I want to go).
Question form you'll hear: wash 3andek...? (do you have...?)
wash kayn...? (is there...?) · ma kaynsh (there isn't).
You'll hear it as advice: 'khassek taxi' — you need a taxi.
